summary: Exact R(2^k−1) for all k ≤ 61 via a dedicated divisor search (for u ≤ v put w = 4Cu−1 = (n+u)/v, sieve-factor n+u for u ≤ √n/2; ~25 CPU-min total; matches the 1e8 census for k ≤ 26 and an independent sympy check R(2^33−1) = 44): R = 0 exactly at k ∈ {2,3,4,5,7,8,13} and R > 0 for every 14 ≤ k ≤ 61 (CERTIFIED; e.g. R = 228 at k = 61, minimum over 30 ≤ k ≤ 61 is 22 at k = 31). Mechanism (PROVED, elementary): no (★) solution n = 4Cuv−u−v of a Mersenne n has u or v in B_k = {1,2} ∪ {2^i+1 : i ≡ k (mod 2)}, because then the needed divisor w ≡ −1 (mod 4u) of n+u is an odd divisor of 2^k, of 2^k+1 (prime factors ≡ 1 mod 4, or ≡ 1,3 mod 8 for k odd) or of 2^{k−i}+1 with k−i even (all odd divisors ≡ 1 mod 4). Residue-matched controls n = 2^k−1+840j (200 per k ≤ 44, 40 per k ≤ 50) get 23% of R from min(u,v) ∈ B_k, and Mersenne R averages 0.70 × the control mean (k = 14..50; median percentile 0.18), so the zeros are this structural ~25–30% depletion plus small-n fluctuation (control means ≈ 9–14 at k ≤ 13), not a persistent obstruction.
not_done: The residual depletion beyond B_k (0.70 observed vs ≈0.77 predicted) is not explained; controls count only min(u,v) ∈ B_k, so the B_k share is a slight undercount; k > 61 not run.
next: Only if wanted: split R(2^k−1) by u to find the remaining structurally depleted u-classes (e.g. u with u−1 = 2^i·s, small s).

summary: PROVED replacement (memo §Z1597): for S_z(C)=sum_{q≤z,q∤4p}1[q|4Cp+1], A=sum 1/q and m=#q, the mean square is ≤A+(m²+2Am)/X, hence ≤A+3/sqrt(X) at z=X^(1/4); for A>5 this bounds the poor fraction by (A+3/sqrt(X))/(A−5)², uniformly in p. The requested unrestricted full-omega bound centered at log log(Xp) is false by CRT plus Linnik, and no Brun-strength bound is claimed. Richness alone therefore does not make a level likely to certify in this range.

No uniform full-omega variance theorem in a restricted polylog(p) regime and no explicit Brun-strength X(log log X)^5/log X bound; the proved small-prime bound is weaker and vacuous at X=4096.

summary: The CUDA port cannot be built or benchmarked here: the machine has only an AMD Radeon 890M iGPU (no CUDA/nvcc; Vulkan only). Instead the census kernel itself was benchmarked and accelerated on CPU: levels C = 1, 2, 3 are decided by a segmented sieve, since (ℤ/4C)^* has exponent 2 for 4C | 24, so −1 is a divisor residue of 4Cp+1 iff it lies in the subgroup generated by its prime factors' residues (PROVED, elementary); only the ≈2.3 % of primes unresolved at C ≤ 3 fall back to trial division. On 2·10⁷-wide windows at 10¹⁰, 10¹¹, 10¹² the per-prime Cmin output is byte-identical to scripts/z52d_p2_SK2_cmin_seg.c and 3.1×, 4.9×, 5.0× faster (1.3/1.9/3.1 s vs 4.2/9.2/15.5 s). With it the C-form census was extended from 10¹⁰ to 5·10¹⁰ (832 298 890 primes ≡ 1 mod 4, 53 CPU-min): every prime has a certificate (CERTIFIED), Cmin = 1 for 81.7 %, and the only prime with Cmin > 3000 is 35 848 375 369 (Cmin = 3632, u = 33, B = 74 774, verified; R = 12).
not_done: No GPU kernel was written or benchmarked (no CUDA device). The census beyond 5·10¹⁰ was not run: the sieve version projects to ≈35 CPU-h for 10¹⁰–10¹², which is beyond the cap, and the trial-division fallback still dominates its cost.
next: Extend the sieve to the non-exponent-2 levels C = 4, 5 (by storing factor lists rather than residue masks); that removes most of the fallback cost and should bring 10¹² within a few CPU-h, without a GPU.

summary: Literature lookup completed: Folding π (arXiv:2403.09277, §3) identifies Fujimoto folds as L(t)=t/2 and R(t)=(t+1)/2, cycling numerators by inverse doubling modulo an odd denominator, not as Egyptian-fraction summands. PROVED: three such folds give (t+j)/8, so a three-fold fixed point has denominator dividing 7; from a dyadic starting crease all finite outputs remain dyadic. Consequently '4/p in three folds' is neither exact for general p nor equivalent to three unit fractions; no Egyptian-fraction connection was found in the targeted search.
not_done: No claim about unrestricted origami axioms; the obstruction concerns only Fujimoto edge-to-crease bisections.

summary: Assembled complete sibling counts from repo witness tables: S(n,−4) has 6/99999 failures through 10^5, Gaussian ES_Q1 has 6/39175 through norm 10^6, and 8/n has 6/2999 through 3000. Its stationary infinite-tail P(any ES counterexample beyond 10^18)=1 is forced by the model’s positive-rate support, not by arithmetic evidence; adding an independent zero-rate ES spike leaves the answer at its arbitrary prior (0.9/0.5/0.1 in the sensitivity run). Thus the fit is completed, but finite heterogeneous sibling tables do not identify a defensible real-world posterior for ES.

summary: Defined the colored additive decomposition operad on positive rationals: every three-unit-fraction decomposition factors through a rational two-term residual, but unit-fraction-only binary refinements require a mergeable pair. summary: PROVED source check: Gupta–Murty (1984), Theorem and Lemmas 1–4, give ≥δX/log²X primes for one of 13 candidates, using the O(Y^(4/3)) small-subgroup bound and the survivor inequality 7>2·3. The ES union is W_J(p)=Σ_(a,C)∈J 1[p≡−a mod(4aC−1)], with #hits≥(ΣW_J)²/ΣW_J², but their subgroup argument supplies neither these moments nor fixed-p positivity. FIXED_MODULUS_SHOTS.md §3.3 already performs the decisive transplant: ‘In ES the set at r is A_r, of r-density ≤ τ₃(k)/r = r^{−1+o(1)}’; §6.1 bounds the available certifying moduli by O(p²). Thus the required bounded exponent-box membership and finite search range are not the primitive-root hypotheses.

summary: PROVED source check: Pintz–Ruzsa II (2020), Theorem 1 and Lemma 6, give K=8 unconditionally and |Σ_(j≤L)e(2^jα)|<0.789401L outside measure ≪N^(−3/5)L^(−100); part I (2003) supplies the lemma and K=7 on GRH. For an ES line with fixed a,b and H consecutive C-values, its exact Fourier sum has modulus H at α=k/(4ab) and ≥0.99H on a union of measure ≥1/(100H). Hence the proposed uniform lacunary large-value estimate fails on the short lines H=polylog N present in the ES range; long-line geometric-sum decay alone supplies no minor-arc error below the expected log²p count. No ES exceptional-set exponent follows (memo §Z2082).

summary: PROVED: ES letters M(k)=[[k,−1],[1,0]] have determinant one, so no product is zero over Z or modulo any m>1. Reviewed the PCP-to-mortality reduction: it introduces a singular projector E11 to turn a zero entry into a zero matrix, a generator absent from ES. CERTIFIED: M(2),M(3) generate all SL2(F_p) for each of the 10 odd primes p≤31, so unrestricted modular-prefix pruning is vacuous; exhaustive length-three residues have p²−p+1 zero-(1,1)-entry targets and sign sum p(−1/p), agreeing exactly with the derived formulas. Modular zero entry is attainable, unlike mortality, and does not force the integer entry to equal p.
not_done: No bounded-height search speed benchmark; determinant invariant settles mortality for all lengths.
next: For actual pruning use remaining-length/height bounds, not zero-product invariants.

summary: PROVED source check: Montgomery–Vaughan (1975), Theorem 1 and §§2–3, give E_G(X)<X^(1−δ), using prime-pair major/minor arcs and zero-density input, not an ES theorem. An ES decomposition R=M+r with M≥c log²N would need Σ|r|²≪N log⁴N exp(−c'(log N)^θ) to yield exponent θ; the Goldbach theorem supplies no such restricted-divisor residual bound.
